doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Guests and tunes on Textures versus By Arrangement

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That instrumentation has a particular sound, I guess. The brass choir stuff. I think the tune, You were having a circus dance.
I think that’s what you ended up calling it.
I guess I just wonder where some ideas like that come from.
Is it the timbre of an instrument or the range…?
I imagine or… Is the vocal group on that one, too?
Yeah. Oh, yeah, I had a Russ Freeman tune that I always loved — The Wind.
Well, actually, that was on the second CD. That was on By Arrangement.
Oh, it was By Arrangement, I see.
Okay. Do you have the names of them down there?
And Ragman and… I’ll think of it. I have the people but not the tunes’ titles on that.
Well, just tell me the people and I’ll…
Well, the people like… that was with Pat Metheny was a guest on one track.
And Greg Osby was a guest on one track.
Oh, Greg did The Wind, though, didn’t he?
He did that, as well, but he was on Textures, also.
So there was a tune of an original.

Okay, sure. Yeah. Anyway, yeah, I feel good about that record, about the writing I did. And I told you, people at Telarc were dubious so I did it. I didn’t even charge them, as I recall, just… ‘cause I just wanted to get it done so…
